Can I share directly?

entries.title: PDF redaction
entries.headline: Redact a PDF {for real, then check it.}
entries.metaTitle: Redact PDFs properly in your browser, with a verify pass
entries.description: Black out text and pictures so they are removed from the file, not just covered, then re-open the saved copy to check. On your device, nothing uploaded.
entries.tagline: Removes what is under the boxes, then verifies
entries.summary: Draw boxes over what must go, or find sensitive data first. Redact and verify makes a new copy with the covered content removed, then opens that copy again and checks that nothing from under the boxes is left. Your original is not changed.
does: Draw boxes on any page, or add the matches from Find sensitive data
By default, pages with boxes are rebuilt as a picture of the page, so nothing under a box can be copied or recovered; their text can no longer be selected
Optional: keep other text selectable where a box covers only plain text
A verify report: the saved file is opened again and searched, and each box is checked to be solid black
Choose picture quality (Standard, High or Best) and an optional label such as REDACTED
steps: Open the PDF, choose Protect, then Hide information for good.
Draw boxes over what to hide, or use Find sensitive data to mark it.
Choose Redact and verify, read the report, and download the new copy.
entries.privacy: The file is redacted and checked on this device and never uploaded. Your original stays as it is; the redacted copy is a new file.
faq: Why not just draw a black box?
A box drawn on top can be moved or deleted, and the text under it can still be copied. Redaction removes that content from the file.
What does “verified” check?

The saved copy is opened again. It checks that the page count is unchanged, that no text is left under a box, that the hidden words are not stored anywhere in the file, that every box is solid black and that no earlier version is inside. If a check fails it says so and tells you not to send the file. It does not replace reading the result yourself.
Why can I not select text on a redacted page?

Pages with boxes become pictures by default, so nothing under a box can be recovered. Pages without boxes stay as they were. The option to keep other text selectable keeps text only where a box covers plain text.
Can a redaction be undone after saving?
No. Keep your original if you might need it. A PDF locked with a password has to be unlocked first.

does: Who made it, with what software, and when
Comments, attached files, form answers and links to outside addresses
Text you cannot see: invisible, white on white, off the page, or under a picture or shape
Earlier versions and unused leftovers still inside the file
Page previews, and camera or location details in pictures
steps: Open the PDF, choose Protect, then What does this PDF reveal?
Read the report, grouped by kind of detail.
Remove what you do not want to send, or all of it, and download the cleaned copy.
entries.privacy: The check runs on this device. Nothing is uploaded.
faq: Does removing this change the pages?
No. It removes data around the pages, not the content you see. The check reads the file as you opened it, not later edits in the studio.
Is every hidden item found?
The common ones are. An unusual file may hold something the check does not recognise, so read important files yourself too.
What about a password-protected PDF?
The details can be read in some cases, but they can only be removed once the password has been taken off the file.

entries.title: Is this PDF safe to open?
entries.headline: Check a PDF {before you open it elsewhere.}
entries.metaTitle: Check a PDF for scripts, embedded files and auto actions
entries.description: Look inside a PDF for scripts, automatic actions, attached files and outside links without running any of them. Not a virus scan. On your device.
entries.tagline: Looks for scripts, automatic actions and attached programs
entries.summary: Reads the inside of a PDF for scripts, actions that run on their own, attached files and links to outside addresses, and reports what it finds in plain language. Nothing in the file is run.
does: Scripts and actions that run when the file opens
Attached files, including programs
Links to outside addresses
Tricks such as disguised names, extra data after the end of the file and earlier versions inside
steps: Open the PDF, choose Protect, then Is it safe to open?
Read the verdict and each finding.
If something is flagged, make a safe copy: active content is removed and attached files are left out. The pages stay the same.
entries.privacy: The file is only read. Nothing in it is run and nothing is uploaded.
faq: Is this a virus scanner?
No. It reports risky features of a PDF, such as scripts and automatic actions. It does not replace security software.
Does it open or run the file?
No. The file is read as data. Nothing inside it is executed.
What does the safe copy change?
It removes active content and leaves out attached files. The pages look the same.

does: Removes scripts, automatic actions and attached files

Prepare the copy, read the checks and download it.

faq: Will people still be able to fill in the form?
Not with the default setting. Flattening makes the current answers part of the page. Turn it off to keep the form.
Does it redact?
No. What is visible on the page stays. Use redaction to remove content from the page.
Does it work on a password-protected PDF?
Not directly. Take the password off the file first, then clean it.

Yes, when you ask: it reads the scanned pages on this device first, and leaves those matches for you to check.
Will it find everything?
It finds common patterns and the words you give it. Always read the document yourself as well.
Does finding something hide it?
No. Nothing is hidden until you add the boxes and choose Redact and verify.

It cannot be recovered, not by LocalEditor and not by anyone else. Keep the password safe, and keep your original.
Can it remove a password I do not know?
No. To remove a password you have to type the current one.
Will every PDF app open the file?
AES-256 is the default and AES-128 is offered for older apps. Open the protected copy once with the password before you send it.

Yes, if you choose: from a column, or built from a pattern. Keep your own list of them, since a lost password cannot be recovered.

From the columns you choose, so each file can carry the person’s name or ID.
